summary: The Center for Responsible Technology argues that E-Rate funding has negatively impacted educational outcomes and youth mental health over the past three decades, and that closing the digital divide led to worse educational outcomes and increased mental health issues. The CRT calls for reevaluating how E-Rate funding incentivizes technological use and contributing to these problems. The claim opposes limiting or sunsetting E-Rate funding, citing potential cost savings from reducing screen time and technology spending in schools. The comment opposes conditionally tying E-Rate funding to screen-time limits and parental autonomy, arguing for screen-free or screen-reduced education to protect student health and learning. It cites evidence on the harms of excessive screen time and the need for clear educational purposes in technology use. The comment also calls for blocking recreational screen time on funded networks and expunging third-party owned devices from school use. The comment opposes tying E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes, arguing that schools should not be required to do so and that parents should have the right to opt their children out of screen-based instruction.
